$doc: Every setting the app has, declared once: its default, its kind, and
where the settings sheet shows it. The store reads the defaults from here
and the sheet renders rows from here, so adding a setting is one entry in
SETTINGS plus its two strings in the locale catalog under
`settings.<section>.<key>`. A choice may carry `costs` beside its
`options`, one per option in the same order, for when what an option costs
differs from its neighbors'; an empty string is no badge. A `dev` setting
is in the kernel's table in every build and offered only under a
development one; the shell's production bundle carries SETTINGS_SHIPPED,
the table without them, in SETTINGS' place.
A choice's `options` names one of the lists below, and the option crosses
and is held as its index there; only storage keeps it by name. A setting
is numbered by its place in SETTINGS (the kernel's SettingKey), which is
what crosses for it. An `index` is a place in a list kept elsewhere — the
person and the pet are by theirs in variant.json — and crosses as itself.
The sheet's sections, in the order they are shown. `character` is not a
section of the sheet at all — its two settings are picked from the
drawer's Character tab (feature/character/picker.tsx), and `world`'s from the
buttons floating over the world (feature/world/ui/control/).
How many device pixels the world is drawn at to a CSS pixel.
auto  — the device's, at most two, lowered while the frames run over
their budget — the display's interval, no tighter than a
sixtieth of a second — and raised again once they have room
(crates/client/kernel/src/view/frame/resolution.rs).
fixed — the device's, at most two, whatever the frames cost.
low   — one.
Which controller makes the camera's pose.
orbit — third person: the camera turns about the focus, its
radius ahead of the eye, and a drag moves the focus.
free  — first person: the eye is the focus and turns in place;
a drag walks it as the orbit's center walks, the eye at its
height over where the walk stands.
What terrain does to the camera.
through — nothing. The eye goes wherever the controls put it, ground
included, where the terrain shell has no inward-facing
geometry and the scene reads inside out.
stop    — a control goes as far as it asked or as far as it can.
Nothing moves on its own; a zoom into a hill stops short.
climb   — dist is always granted and the *view* pitches up instead,
as far as straight down, so every zoom stays
reachable at the cost of an angle nobody asked for.
How many of the eye's rays the GPU casts for the screen's cells.
cells — one a cell of the camera grid.
half  — one every second CSS pixel each way.
full  — one a CSS pixel, whatever the device draws it at.
Where the ambient occlusion comes from.
off    — none.
corner — a chunk shades its own corners from the face bits the edge
shading reads (crates/client/render/src/frame/shader/chunk.wgsl):
the floor along a cube and the inside of a corner, over about
half a cell, scaling the ambient and hemisphere light only.
A few fragment ops behind a uniform.
screen — N8AO
(crates/client/render/src/gpu/ao.rs): the world's depth drawn
once more, the occlusion sampled from it at half resolution,
denoised, and applied to every lit surface as a warm dark
tint. Five passes and 11 bytes a pixel.
Ground color from the art pack (four taps of the layer array per
fragment) instead of the flat per-instance average. The chunk shader's
`frame.low_spec` is this, inverted.
Low because the four taps are all of it: fill rate, which scales with
the screen and not with the world, and nothing else — no geometry, no
pass of its own, and no work off the GPU past an atlas the client
already holds.
It sources the chunks: the shader samples a leaf's layer or does not,
but a tier over it carries one color and no layer to sample, so which
color that is was baked in (mesh/chunk.rs).
Procedurally scattered decor only; what the player placed stays.
Med because it is models rather than a shading term: a chunk builds its
decor and the frame draws it, so what it costs follows what is in view.
It has been the frame's own bottleneck — 20260912-what-to-render-when.md
reads GPU p95 24.1 ms with 2.26 M decor triangles and 15% of moving
frames missing a vsync — and the projected-size criterion holds it to
the nearest tier without making far decor cheap, the impostor tier that
would being decided and not built. The badge is an ordering, and this is
the one to reach for before any shading term.
The cumulus' models and the altocumulus and cirrus sheets
(crates/client/kernel/src/scene/environment/cloud.rs, crates/client/render/src/gpu/clouds.rs).
Med as decor is: models in view, and a pass over the screen for the sheets.
The places' badges over the world, from the published places tiles.
Rotate-drag and pinch stop writing polar; azimuth is unaffected.
Off by default: the tilt is the one control a view from above is expected to
have, and locking it reads as the app being stuck.
Which controller makes the camera's pose; CAMERA_MODES says each. To
first person the person stands at the focus, the eye at its
height over the ground; to third the focus is laid on the ground
and the eye steps back by the radius.

The focus stands on what supports it and a pan takes the lowest way over what is in it (navigation/support.rs). Off, a pan keeps the center's height and passes through anything; a tap still stands it on the surface it struck.
What the camera does when the controls would put it underground; ORBIT_OBSTACLE_MODES says each.
Darkens cube edges that border open air (crates/client/render/src/frame/shader/chunk.wgsl).
A few fragment ops behind a uniform; the shader is the same either way.
A uniform on an already-compiled shader term; not a pass.
corner, the occlusion a voxel world gets from its own geometry with no
screen-space pass; screen, N8AO's screen-space pass, the costliest of
the three. AO_MODES says each.
The sun's shadow map (crates/client/render/src/gpu/shadow.rs): the world drawn once more
from the sun each frame, depth only, and a 3x3 compare per fragment;
16 MB of map on a desktop, 4 on a phone.
The pixels the world is filled at, the GPU's largest cost: two to a
CSS pixel is four times the fragments of one. RESOLUTION_MODES says each.
Where the camera and the pointer are, read live (profiler/summary.rs, its view section).
The profiler's panel, with the profiler recording while it is on (profiler/log.rs `profiler_follow`).

Marks for the focus and the cell it floors to, and rings in the level, the view's upright and the north–south planes (scene/indicator/frame_gizmo.rs); and the drawn pieces, the goal's pieces nothing drawn covers by why, the tiles and the shards (scene/indicator/coverage_gizmo.rs).

The camera grid over the screen, the one the rays are cast through, a cell a ray, and the chunks tinted by how many zooms a face is off the one the grid's rule draws there: green at it, blue finer, red coarser (scene/indicator/camera_gizmo.rs).
female-2, by its number in variant.json's person keys.
chick, by its number in variant.json's pet keys.
How many rays the GPU casts for the screen's cells (scene/cast.rs); RAY_DENSITIES says each.
Each ray's cell coloured by the nodes its descent asked the world, on one fixed log ramp up to 1024 (crates/client/render/src/frame/shader/screen_cells.wgsl).
